ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reproducing episodic test-time adaptation methods under one checkpoint
PROPOSAL: Rerun TPT, C-TPT and DiffTPT from released code with a single CLIP ViT-B/16 checkpoint and a fixed prompt template, on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and 10 fine-grained datasets. Use 64 augmented views per image and the same confidence-selection rule of 10 % in all methods. Report top-1 accuracy across 3 seeds, and the gap between the reproduced numbers and the figures in the original papers.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same prompt; an ensemble of 80 templates as a stronger unadapted reference; methods run with their original authors' prompts, to measure how far the setup alone moves the numbers.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Reproduced gains over zero-shot should be 1 to 3 points smaller than reported for most methods. It could fail if the released code already fixes the setup and the gap is close to 0.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Episodic adaptation reproduced with a ViT-L/14 backbone on ImageNet and its variants
PROPOSAL: Rerun TPT, C-TPT and DiffTPT from released code with a CLIP ViT-L/14 checkpoint and a fixed prompt template, on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch. Use 64 augmented views per image and the confidence-selection rule of 10 % in all methods. Repeat the evaluation from 5 seeds, and report top-1 accuracy with the gap between the reproduced numbers and the original papers.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP ViT-L/14 with the same prompt; entropy minimisation on a single view as a lightweight reference; a ViT-B/16 rerun of the weakest method as a size contrast.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Reproduced gains over zero-shot should be 1 to 3 points smaller than reported for the larger backbone as well. It could fail if the strong backbone leaves so little room that the methods sit within noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online cache methods on ImageNet under reshuffled streams
PROPOSAL: Run TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 as online adapters on the ImageNet validation stream, reshuffling the sample order with 5 seeds. Record top-1 accuracy as a running curve over the first 1000, 5000 and 50000 samples, and compare the final accuracy with the unadapted model. Fix the prompt template and the cache capacity across methods so that differences reflect the algorithms.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same template; a frozen cache filled with the first 100 samples; a cache with shuffled labels and the same size, to check that gains depend on content.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Gains over zero-shot should be 0.5 to 1.5 points and settle after about 10000 samples. It could fail if stream order moves the final accuracy by more than the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online cache methods compared across datasets, backbones and stream orders
PROPOSAL: Run TDA and DMN-ZS as online adapters with CLIP ViT-B/16 and RN50 on ImageNet and 10 fine-grained datasets, reshuffling the sample order with 3 seeds. Record top-1 accuracy as a running curve over the first 1000, 5000 and 50000 samples and compare the final accuracy with the unadapted model. Fix the prompt template across methods, and repeat with other cache capacities.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same template; a frozen cache filled with the first 100 samples; a cache with shuffled labels and the same size.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Gains over zero-shot should be 0.5 to 1.5 points on most datasets and settle after about 10000 samples. It could fail if stream order moves the final accuracy by more than the gain, or if smaller datasets never fill the cache.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration and selective prediction after test-time adaptation
PROPOSAL: Measure expected calibration error, negative log-likelihood and risk-coverage curves for TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch, then score out-of-distribution detection with maximum softmax probability using ImageNet-A against ImageNet, with 15 confidence bins for calibration. Fix the prompt template, use 3 seeds, and report bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same template; temperature scaling fitted on a held-out ImageNet split of 5000 images as a calibration reference; the methods with their confidence thresholds swept to separate the effect of selection from adaptation.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: Accuracy-oriented methods should raise calibration error on at least 2 of the 4 sets while adding 1 to 3 points of accuracy. It could fail if calibration shifts are smaller than the bootstrap interval.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration error after episodic adaptation with a ViT-L/14 backbone
PROPOSAL: Measure expected calibration error, negative log-likelihood and selective prediction curves for TPT, C-TPT and TDA with CLIP ViT-L/14 on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch, using 15 confidence bins and a bin-free estimator to check that the conclusion does not depend on binning. Fix the prompt template, rerun with 5 seeds, and report bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples with the accuracy change for the same runs.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP ViT-L/14 with the same template; temperature scaling fitted on a held-out ImageNet split; a ViT-B/16 rerun of the whole pipeline as a size contrast.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: Adaptation should raise calibration error on at least 2 of the 4 sets while adding 1 to 3 points of accuracy. It could fail if the shifts are smaller than the bootstrap interval for the larger model, or if the ranking of methods changes with the binning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation beyond CLIP on 3 vision-language families
PROPOSAL: Port TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS to SigLIP ViT-B/16, EVA-CLIP ViT-B/16 and an OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 trained on LAION, using the same prompt template and augmentation views as the CLIP runs. Evaluate top-1 accuracy on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch and 10 fine-grained datasets, over 3 seeds, and compare the gain over zero-shot against the CLIP gain for the same method, plus the failure cases on the 10 most affected classes.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot accuracy of the models with their own recommended prompt and with the shared prompt; a prompt ensemble of 80 templates; the CLIP ViT-B/16 gains reproduced under the same code path.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gains should shrink by about 1 point on models with stronger zero-shot accuracy such as SigLIP. It could fail if differences in the text tower make the shared prompt unfair to one family.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptation gains of 3 vision-language families on large backbones
PROPOSAL: Port TPT, C-TPT and TDA to SigLIP ViT-L/14, EVA-CLIP ViT-L/14 and an OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 trained on LAION, using the same prompt template and augmentation views as the CLIP runs. Evaluate top-1 accuracy on ImageNet and ImageNet-A, over 5 seeds with bootstrap intervals, and compare the gain over zero-shot against the CLIP ViT-L/14 gain for the same method, plus a rerun at 2 prompt templates.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot accuracy of the models with their recommended prompt and with the shared prompt; a prompt ensemble of 80 templates; the CLIP ViT-L/14 gains reproduced under the same code path.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gains should shrink by about 1 point on models with stronger zero-shot accuracy such as SigLIP. It could fail if differences in the text tower make the shared prompt unfair to a family.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation on top of prompt-tuned checkpoints
PROPOSAL: Train CoOp, MaPLe and PromptSRC with 16 shots on ImageNet using CLIP ViT-B/16 and apply TPT, C-TPT and TDA on top, evaluated on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and ImageNet-V2 and in a base-to-novel split of 10 datasets. Report top-1 accuracy from 3 tuning seeds and compare the combined gain with the sum of the separate gains to see whether the two kinds of adaptation add up or conflict.
CONTROLS: The tuned models without test-time adaptation; test-time adaptation on untuned CLIP; a tuned model whose prompts are replaced by the hand-written template before adaptation; a tuned model with 4 shots in place of 16.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The combined gain should be smaller than the sum of the separate gains by about 1 to 2 points. It could fail if tuned prompts overfit to base classes and make adaptation conflict on novel ones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation on repeatedly tuned checkpoints with a ViT-L/14 backbone
PROPOSAL: Train CoOp and MaPLe with 16 shots on ImageNet using CLIP ViT-L/14 and apply TPT and TDA on top, evaluated on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and ImageNet-V2. Repeat the tuning from 5 seeds, and for the checkpoints report top-1 accuracy and compare the combined gain with the sum of the separate gains to see whether the two kinds of adaptation add up or conflict.
CONTROLS: Tuned models without test-time adaptation; test-time adaptation on untuned CLIP ViT-L/14; a tuned model with 8 shots instead of 16; a tuned model scored after 2 further epochs of tuning.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The combined gain should be smaller than the sum of the separate gains by about 1 to 2 points. It could fail if tuning on the large backbone leaves too little room for adaptation to show up in the accuracy of the checkpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How much progress adaptation methods made since the earliest ones
PROPOSAL: Collect per-sample predictions from reproduced runs of entropy minimisation, TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet and its 4 variants. Estimate the gain of a method over zero-shot with paired bootstrap intervals from 10000 resamples, and test whether the ranking of recent methods against the earliest ones survives prompt changes drawn from 5 templates. Report the share of reported progress that remains.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same prompts; a permutation null with 1000 shuffles of method labels per sample; the numbers claimed in the papers; ranking by mean accuracy alone as a naive reading.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: The gap between the earliest and the latest method should shrink by 30 to 50 % relative to reported figures. It could fail if differences between methods fall inside the bootstrap interval so that no ranking is supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progress of adaptation methods remeasured on fine-grained datasets with repeated runs
PROPOSAL: Rerun entropy minimisation, TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet, its 4 variants and 10 fine-grained datasets, keeping per-sample predictions from 3 seeds. Estimate the gain of a method over zero-shot with paired bootstrap intervals from 10000 resamples, and test whether the ranking of recent methods against the earliest ones survives prompt changes drawn from 5 templates. Report the share of progress that remains.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same prompts; a permutation null that shuffles method labels per sample; the numbers claimed in the papers; ranking by mean accuracy alone; a ranking restricted to the datasets where the variance is lowest.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: The gap between the earliest and the latest method should shrink by 30 to 50 % relative to reported figures on most datasets. It could fail if differences between methods fall inside the bootstrap interval so that no ranking is supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online adaptation under class-ordered and bursty streams
PROPOSAL: Evaluate TDA, DMN-ZS and an entropy-minimisation baseline with CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch under 3 stream orders: shuffled, sorted by class and bursty with runs of 50 samples of one class. Report accuracy by quartile of the stream and the final accuracy over 5 seeds, and track how fast the memory fills with wrong labels, so that stability can be read from the curves, and fit a regression of accuracy on the position in the stream to quantify drift.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same template; the methods with memory reset at intervals of 1000 samples; a variant keeping only high-confidence entries; the shuffled stream as the neutral reference.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Sorted and bursty streams should cost online methods 2 to 5 points relative to shuffled ones, while zero-shot stays flat. It could fail if methods with a confidence filter are unaffected by order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stream-order effects on online adaptation across datasets and backbones
PROPOSAL: Run TDA, DMN-ZS and an entropy-minimisation baseline with CLIP ViT-B/16 and RN50 over ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and 10 fine-grained datasets, feeding samples in shuffled, class-sorted and bursty order with bursts of 50 same-class images. Log quartile-wise and final accuracy from 3 seeds, follow how quickly wrong labels accumulate in the memory to read stability off the curves, and fit accuracy against the position in the stream to quantify drift.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP with the same template; memory reset at intervals of 1000 samples; a variant that stores only confident entries; shuffled order as the neutral reference; a run with labels of the stored entries corrected by an oracle.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Class-sorted and bursty orders should lower online accuracy by 2 to 5 points against shuffled order while zero-shot stays flat. It could fail if confidence-filtered methods ignore order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial and group robustness after test-time adaptation
PROPOSAL: Attack CLIP ViT-B/16 with 10-step projected gradient descent at a perturbation of 1/255 on ImageNet validation images, then apply TPT, C-TPT and TDA to the attacked inputs. Report robust accuracy, worst-class accuracy and the accuracy of the 100 most frequent classes against the 100 least frequent, from 3 seeds of attack initialisation, using the fixed prompt template.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP under the same attack; the same attack with the adaptation methods aware of it; a random-noise perturbation of matched norm; clean accuracy of the methods as a reference.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Adaptation should lift clean accuracy by 1 to 3 points but leave robust accuracy within 1 point of zero-shot. It could fail if augmentation views partly undo the perturbation and raise robust accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of adapted models across attacks, corruptions and class groups
PROPOSAL: Attack CLIP ViT-B/16 and RN50 with 10-step projected gradient descent at a perturbation of 1/255 and evaluate on ImageNet-C across corruption types and severities, then apply TPT, C-TPT and TDA to the attacked inputs. Report robust accuracy, worst-class accuracy and the accuracy of the 100 most frequent classes against the 100 least frequent, over 5 seeds, using the fixed prompt template.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP under the same attack and corruptions; the adaptation methods run on clean inputs; a random-noise perturbation of matched norm; clean accuracy of the methods as a reference.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Adaptation should lift clean accuracy by 1 to 3 points but leave robust accuracy within 1 point of zero-shot. It could fail if augmentation views partly undo the perturbation and raise robust accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt sensitivity of test-time adaptation methods
PROPOSAL: Compare TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 on ImageNet, ImageNet-A and ImageNet-R under 20 hand-written prompt templates and 3 sets of class descriptions generated by a language model. Measure the spread of accuracy across prompts for a method, and test whether gains over zero-shot persist when the starting prompt is weak, using 3 seeds, a mixed-effects model with prompt as a random factor, and bootstrap intervals for the spread.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP under the same prompts; an ensemble of 80 templates; a method with the prompt picked on the test set as an upper reference; a template with shuffled class names as a floor.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Spread across prompts should be 2 to 4 points for zero-shot and smaller for methods that adapt the prompt. It could fail if prompt choice explains less variance than seed and the model finds no effect.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt sensitivity measured on ImageNet with a ViT-L/14 backbone
PROPOSAL: Compare TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-L/14 on ImageNet under 100 prompt templates sampled from a pool of hand-written and model-generated ones. Measure the spread of accuracy across prompts for a method, and test whether gains over zero-shot persist when the starting prompt is weak, rerunning from 5 seeds and fitting a mixed-effects model with prompt as a random factor.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP ViT-L/14 under the same prompts; an ensemble of 80 templates; the method with the prompt picked on the test set as an upper reference; a template with shuffled class names as a floor.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Spread across prompts should be 2 to 4 points for zero-shot and smaller for methods that adapt the prompt. It could fail if prompt choice explains less variance than seed and the model finds no effect.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Accuracy per second of test-time adaptation methods
PROPOSAL: Measure wall-clock time, peak memory and accuracy of TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch and ImageNet-V2, at batch sizes 1 and 8 on a fixed device. Draw the frontier of accuracy gain against time per sample over 5 timing repeats, and report which methods stay on it when the backbone grows, noting the memory cost of the 64 views for the episodic methods.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP at the same batch sizes; TPT with 16 views in place of 64; a prompt ensemble of 80 templates as a cheap non-adaptive way to gain accuracy; a warm-up run discarded before timing.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Episodic methods should cost 10 to 60 times the time per sample of zero-shot and fall off the frontier for ViT-L/14. It could fail if caching methods match their gain at nearly zero added time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Accuracy per second of adaptation methods across backbones and datasets
PROPOSAL: Measure wall-clock time, peak memory and accuracy of TPT, C-TPT, TDA and DMN-ZS with CLIP ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14 and RN50 on ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and 10 fine-grained datasets, at batch sizes 1 and 8 on a fixed device. Draw the frontier of accuracy gain against time per sample over 20 timing repeats, and report which methods stay on it when the backbone grows.
CONTROLS: Zero-shot CLIP at the same batch sizes; TPT with 16 views in place of 64; a prompt ensemble of 80 templates; a warm-up run discarded before timing; a run under a second process loading the device.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Episodic methods should cost 10 to 60 times the time per sample of zero-shot and fall off the frontier for ViT-L/14. It could fail if caching methods match their gain at nearly zero added time.
